bill.title: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Federal Communications Commission relating to "Addressing the Homework Gap Through the E-Rate Program".
bill.officialSummary: This joint resolution nullifies the final rule issued by the Federal Communications Commission titled Addressing the Homework Gap Through the E-Rate Program and published on August 20, 2024. The rule permits schools and libraries participating in the Schools and Libraries Universal Service Support program (E-Rate) to purchase discounted Wi-Fi hotspots and associated mobile connectivity service for off-premises use by students, school staff, and library patrons. Under the rule, E-Rate participants must implement acceptable use policies that require hotspots to be used primarily for educational purposes.

classification.plainSummary: This resolution would overturn a Federal Communications Commission rule that allows schools and libraries to use E-Rate program funds to purchase Wi-Fi hotspots and mobile internet service for students and patrons to use at home. The FCC rule was designed to help students complete homework and access educational resources outside of school buildings. If this resolution passes, that rule would be nullified and schools and libraries would no longer be able to use E-Rate funds for off-campus internet access.

industries.rationale: The bill would eliminate a new revenue stream for wireless carriers and broadband providers who sell hotspots and mobile connectivity services to schools and libraries under the E-Rate program.
The bill would remove schools' and libraries' ability to purchase subsidized internet access equipment for students and patrons, affecting their budgets and service delivery.
The bill would affect manufacturers and vendors of Wi-Fi hotspot devices that would have been purchased through the expanded E-Rate program.

plain.whatItDoes: This joint resolution would cancel the final rule issued by the FCC titled Addressing the Homework Gap Through the E-Rate Program and published on August 20, 2024.
plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who uses a phone, the internet, or a connected device.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in the services and devices you use. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.
plain.source: Reworded from the official summary. Staff at the Congressional Research Service wrote that summary. It is public domain, and the full text of it is further down this page.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
